notes: CONCEPTS C2 lists spi_dat_o as a receive-data exit even though the RTL reuses rtx_engine.sreg for both received data and transmit output.
The FIFO behavior cited for internal FIFO points relies on the supplied black-box rule for neorv32_fifo.

points.reason: The bus data directly determines the transmit word written toward the transmit FIFO, so an unauthorized bus write can alter the payload.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the value on tx_fifo.wdata is stored when tx_fifo.we is asserted, so the FIFO input path can alter the queued transmit payload.
The transmit FIFO word is selected and loaded into rtx_engine.sreg, where an altered queued word changes the transmitted payload.
The output directly exposes the current transmit shift-register bit and forcing it changes the serialized payload.
The sampled serial input is loaded into sdi_sync and then shifted into sreg, so changing spi_dat_i changes the received payload.
This block only forwards the received shift-register value to the FIFO and does not itself expose or modify the received payload.
The FIFO black box buffers the received word, but the RTL shows no direct unauthorized read or modification at this internal point.
A bus read copies rx_fifo.rdata into bus_rsp_o.data, making the received payload readable through the bus response.
The reused shift register is directly exposed on spi_dat_o, so received bits can be observed at the serial output.
A bus write loads ctrl.enable, so the designed access can overwrite the enable setting and disable SPI operation.
The inverse of ctrl.enable clears the receive FIFO, which can discard pending data and prevent normal operation.
By the black-box FIFO rule, asserting the clear input can clear the receive buffer and block queued receive data from operation.
The inverse of ctrl.enable clears the transmit FIFO, discarding queued transfers.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the clear input can empty the transmit buffer and prevent queued transfers.
When ctrl.enable is zero, the clock divider is reset and no SPI clock-enable pulses are generated.
ctrl.enable controls the engine state and disabled operation returns the state machine to its inactive behavior.
The enable term gates irq_o, so clearing the setting can suppress the notification needed for continued service.
The boundary output directly carries ctrl.enable, so changing or withholding it changes the external enable control.
Bus writes load the prescaler, divider and high-speed configuration fields, allowing the settings to be changed to values that disrupt the transfer rate.
The configuration fields determine the clock-source selection, divider comparison and generation of spi_clk_en, so bad settings can withhold or mispace transfer progress.
The generated enable pulse gates every transceiver step, so suppressing or mispacing it can stall the SPI transfer.
The bus data supplies the transmit control word, so an altered bus write can select a different chip-select command.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the control word is stored when written into the transmit FIFO and can therefore be altered before use.
The transceiver loads cs_ctrl from a FIFO word selected by its control bit, so the stored control can select the wrong device or fail to select the intended one.
The block only returns the chip-select status in a bus response and does not itself modify or block chip-select generation.
The control word selects which spi_csn_o bit is driven low, so changing it selects another device or leaves the intended device deselected.
The process computes irq_o from enable, interrupt enables, FIFO status and engine busy state, so altered inputs can create false or missing interrupt notifications.
Bus writes change the interrupt-enable and operational-enable fields that gate or qualify irq_o, allowing false or suppressed notifications.
The FIFO availability status directly participates in the receive interrupt condition, so an altered status can cause a false or missing request.
The FIFO availability and half-full status directly qualify transmit-empty and transmit-level interrupts, so altered status can corrupt or suppress notification.
The busy indication is derived from the engine state and qualifies the idle interrupt, so changing it can create or suppress the notification.
The transceiver state determines rtx_engine.busy, which is used in the idle interrupt condition; changing state can therefore produce or suppress irq_o.
